cases.name: a-run-of-one-row
cases.description: One row is still a row. Engine 1 used to refuse the per-row derivation at count="1" — a build of one row looked to it like the inner call its own loop makes — and fell back to the threaded PRNG, so a single-row run came out different from the same run on engines 2 and 3.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="1" seed="one" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="X"><gen type="regex" value="[a-e]{3}"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{X}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-run-of-one-row-holds-for-numbers-too
cases.description: The same refusal, on a different generator: nothing about it was regex-specific.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="1" seed="one" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="N"><gen type="number" value="1000..9999"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{N}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: the-first-two-rows-of-a-run-are-not-two-runs-of-one
cases.description: count="1" and count="2" draw the same first row. They must: the row's value comes from (seed, column, row) and nothing else, so how many rows follow it cannot change it.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="one" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="X"><gen type="regex" value="[a-e]{3}"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{X}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-mix-case-that-comes-to-one-row
cases.description: A <mix> case is a column of its own, over whichever rows the percentages gave it. When that came to a single row the in-memory engine took the same wrong turn as a count="1" run, and only that row's value differed — the case SELECTION agreed, which is what made it so quiet.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="7" local="en" mode="memory"><mix name="P" percent="34,33"><case><data>A</data></case><case><mix percent="50"><case><gen type="regex" value="[a-e]"/></case><case><data>M</data></case></mix></case><case><data>C</data></case></mix></env><block><line><data>${{P}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-nested-mix-two-levels-down
cases.description: The same shape at a larger count, so the inner case holds more than one row and the arrangement is exercised rather than the single-row edge alone.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="20" seed="7" local="en" mode="memory"><mix name="P" percent="50,25"><case><data>A</data></case><case><mix percent="50"><case><gen type="number" value="10..99"/></case><case><data>M</data></case></mix></case><case><data>C</data></case></mix></env><block><line><data>${{P}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-whole-column-pack-in-a-run-of-one-row
cases.description: A pack generator whose body declares a share is a WHOLE-COLUMN build: its quota is cut from the run, not drawn per row. In a run of count="1" that build holds a single row, and the count was read as "this is a per-row build" — so the body's seed was salted with the row, which a column-wide build must never be. 73 of the 121 bundled whole-column packs answered differently on the in-memory engine than on the streaming ones because of it.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="1" seed="wc" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="A"><gen type="template" value="bangladesh.docs.nid"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{A}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-whole-column-pack-is-the-same-run-at-any-count
cases.description: The same pack over three rows. A whole-column quota does depend on how many rows there are — that is what makes it whole-column — so this pins the arrangement rather than the single value, and it is the case the one above is measured against.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="wc" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="A"><gen type="template" value="bangladesh.docs.nid"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{A}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-whole-column-pack-with-a-compound-body
cases.description: The compound branch of a pack body — one column per field — took the same wrong turn in one implementation and not the others, so it is pinned separately from the plain one.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="1" seed="wc" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="A"><gen type="template" value="cambodia.vehicle.plate"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{A}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-pack-that-names-another-pack
cases.description: `common.internet.email` draws its domain from `common.internet.domain` — a pack body naming a second pack. The inner body must be seeded from the OUTER BODY's seed, not from the run's: seeded from the run it lands on the same value for every row, so a column of addresses came out as one domain repeated behind varying tokens. Three rows, because a single row cannot show a value that fails to move.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="pp" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="E"><gen type="template" value="common.internet.email"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{E}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-pack-that-names-another-pack-with-a-parameter
cases.description: The same, with the outer pack parameterised — `domain=` replaces the sequence that would have drawn from the inner pack. The parameter draws nothing, so everything after it must land exactly where it would have without one.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="pp" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="E"><gen type="template" value="common.internet.email" domain="example.test"/></sequence><sequence name="P"><gen type="template" value="common.internet.email"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{E}} ${{P}}</data></line></block></tdc>
